text:
T.J. Hughes took the long road to Colorado: never drafted, 57 points in 40 games for Michigan last season, then a spot in the Avalanche lineup as a 25-year-old rookie. He has 7 points and a shooting problem that looks temporary. He has put 45 shots on goal, worth 5.78 expected goals (the quality of his chances, measured in goals), and scored twice. His nine-game goalless run came on 3.8 expected goals. Goals tend to follow chances, and we'd expect his to start arriving.

The Hockey Writers ran a piece titled "Avalanche Rookie T.J. Hughes Has More to Offer Than the Numbers Show," and on offense we agree. The other end is the open question. Colorado outshoots opponents with him on the ice at five on five but gives up the better chances: his group gets 46% of the expected goals, about 8 points worse than the team without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, over only six games, hasn't found a clear strength or weakness yet.

His minutes are climbing, close to 16 a night lately, and he has two power-play points. Our range has him at 13 to 28 goals this season.
headline: T.J. Hughes is getting the looks, not the goals
